name: Magnitude-ordered FastTwoSum
definition: For |a|≥|b|, compute s=fl(a+b), z=fl(s−a), e=fl(b−z). Under the stated arithmetic assumptions, a+b=s+e as real numbers.
variables: a,b floating-point operands; s rounded sum; z temporary; e residual; fl working-precision rounding
assumptions: Finite binary IEEE floating-point values, fixed precision, round-to-nearest ties-to-even, gradual underflow, |a|≥|b| and no overflowing intermediate
limitations: Magnitude ordering is a sufficient, not necessary, restriction; the pair is exact in real arithmetic, not necessarily when rounded again; arbitrary operand order, flush-to-zero or reassociation can defeat exactness
failure_conditions: Magnitude ordering absent for this restricted specification
computation: Check magnitude ordering, evaluate the three rounded operations as written, and retain both output components without adding them again

source.citation: Lange and Oishi (2020), A note on Dekker’s FastTwoSum algorithm, Numerische Mathematik 145, 383–403, Theorem 1 and Lemma 1, DOI 10.1007/s00211-020-01114-2. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00211-020-01114-2

application: General numerical residual extraction; no forecasting benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Ordered floating-point pair and declared arithmetic
incompatible_methods: Assuming exactness for arbitrary input ordering
mechanism_note: Magnitude ordering implies the sufficient exponent ordering in the binary format. For binary64, a=1 and b=2^−53 give s=1, z=0 and e=2^−53. A separate unordered counterexample is a=1, b=2^54: s=2^54, z=2^54 and e=0, although the real residual is 1. The halfway subtraction 2^54−1 rounds to 2^54 in ties-to-even. The three-operation ordered variant computes the same real pair identity as the existing general six-operation TwoSum; it is not a distinct statistical model.

name: Scaled sum-of-squares accumulation
definition: Maintain m≥0 and q≥0 with Σx_i²=m²q in exact arithmetic. For each nonzero x let v=|x|; if v>m, update q←1+q(m/v)² and m←v; otherwise q←q+(v/m)². Return m√q.
variables: m maximum magnitude so far; q scaled accumulator; x next term; v absolute value
assumptions: Finite real floating-point inputs, declared working precision and ordered evaluation; start m=q=0, skip zeros, and require finite scaled state and final norm
limitations: The invariant is exact only in real arithmetic; ratios and squares can round or underflow, accumulation can lose small contributions, and an unrepresentable final norm can overflow; this historical one-scale algorithm is not the current three-accumulator safe-scaling implementation
failure_conditions: Invalid negative state or nonzero q with m=0
computation: Initialize m=q=0; skip zero entries, apply the recurrence in one pass, then evaluate m times sqrt(q) without explicitly squaring m; return zero for an empty or all-zero sequence

source.citation: LAPACK 3.1 (2006), DLASSQ auxiliary routine, Netlib source, purpose and executable recurrence. https://netlib.org/lapack/lapack-3.1.1/html/dlassq.f.html

application: General numerical norm evaluation; no forecasting benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Finite numeric sequence and arithmetic format
incompatible_methods: Claiming overflow immunity for unrepresentable final norms
mechanism_note: When a new maximum v appears, v²[1+q(m/v)²]=v²+m²q; otherwise m²[q+(v/m)²]=m²q+v². The induction starts at zero, and the nonzero branch prevents division by zero. Ratios have magnitude at most one, avoiding direct squaring of a large input. This is a scale-changing norm reduction, not the unscaled pairwise or compensated sum of already rounded terms.

name: Dekker binary64 significand splitting
definition: With C=2^27+1 compute t=fl(Ca), h=fl(t−fl(t−a)), l=fl(a−h). Under the stated arithmetic conditions a=h+l exactly with nonoverlapping components.
variables: a binary64 input; C splitting constant; t temporary; h high component; l low component; fl rounded arithmetic
assumptions: Finite binary64 input, round-to-nearest ties-to-even, each arithmetic operation rounded separately in binary64, no overflow or underflow in intermediate arithmetic for this restricted specification
limitations: The initial multiplication can overflow for large a; this specification does not include rescaling or claim exactness with flush-to-zero, reassociation or mixed precision
failure_conditions: Unestablished arithmetic semantics or underflow outside the restricted domain
computation: Use the exact representable constant C, one rounded multiplication and three ordered rounded subtractions; retain h and l separately

source.citation: Ogita, Rump and Oishi (2005), Accurate Sum and Dot Product, SIAM J. Sci. Comput. 26(6), 1955–1988, p. 1961, Algorithm 3.2, DOI 10.1137/030601818. https://ogilab.w.waseda.jp/ogita/math/doc/2005_OgRuOi.pdf

application: General floating-point decomposition into high and low components; no forecasting benefit claimed.
required_inputs: One finite binary64 operand and declared arithmetic
incompatible_methods: Treating split as an unrestricted multiplication residual
mechanism_note: The source establishes the nonoverlapping exact decomposition for its arithmetic model. For a=1+2^−52, the rounded product is C+2^−25, h=1 and l=2^−52. A single input is decomposed into two narrower components, unlike TwoSum on two inputs or FMA extraction of an existing product residual.

name: TwoSum cascaded compensated summation
definition: For n≥1 let p_1=x_1 and c_1=0; for i=2,…,n set (p_i,r_i)=TwoSum(p_(i−1),x_i), c_i=fl(c_(i−1)+r_i); return fl(p_n+c_n).
variables: x_i input terms; p_i running rounded sum; r_i exact local residual; c_i rounded residual accumulation; fl rounding
assumptions: Nonempty finite floating-point sequence, fixed binary working precision, round-to-nearest ties-to-even with gradual underflow, strict TwoSum semantics and no overflow in any intermediate
limitations: The residual accumulation and final addition still round; the result is not a guaranteed correctly rounded or exact sum; cancellation may make relative error large
failure_conditions: Violation of the registered TwoSum arithmetic domain
computation: Apply the registered six-operation TwoSum at each iteration, accumulate each residual separately, and add the two final accumulators once in working precision

source.citation: Ogita, Rump and Oishi (2005), Accurate Sum and Dot Product, p. 1963, Algorithm 4.1 and equation (4.2), DOI 10.1137/030601818. https://ogilab.w.waseda.jp/ogita/math/doc/2005_OgRuOi.pdf

application: General compensated summation of floating-point measurements; no forecasting benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Nonempty finite sequence and declared floating-point arithmetic
incompatible_methods: Claiming exact final accumulation because individual residuals are exact
mechanism_note: Successive exact local identities give Σx_i=p_n+Σ_(i=2)^n r_i in real arithmetic by telescoping; c_n approximates rather than exactly represents the latter sum. The correction is separately accumulated and appended once, unlike Kahan’s feedback into each incoming term. It is conservatively classified in the compensated-summation family, not as an additional distinct algorithm.
